post.description: Tenant administrators only, with a recent sign-in and their own rate budget. Returns the signed payment link for an open, payable invoice (the same link a customer's invoice notice carries) so staff can read it out or show it as a QR code. The link is a bearer capability: it is never cached, logged or audited (the audit row names who and which invoice). It stops working at `expires_at` (a server-side time, 14 days after issue by default and extended by each new link), when it is revoked, and when the invoice is no longer payable. A request takes no body and no idempotency key: a stored receipt would copy the link into a table. One identical 404 answers an invoice that is missing or belongs to another provider; 409 `invoice_not_payable` answers one that is paid, void, written off, part paid, or whose account or service no longer allows payment.

Tenant administrators only, with a recent sign-in, the fail-closed write budget and an `Idempotency-Key`. Kills every payment link ever handed out for this invoice (its link version moves on and the expiry is cleared); a new link must be issued afterwards. It works while a payment is pending (that attempt has its own gateway session). The audit row names the invoice, the actor, the new version and the reason, never a link; a reason that holds a link or token is refused (422 `revoke_reason_invalid`).

post.description: Captures a registration for one SIM at the counter and queues it for verification; it returns at once and the counter serves the next customer. The identity goes through the KYC module (consent channel `store`). The ICCID is kept only as a keyed fingerprint and its last four digits. Refuses a SIM that already has a registration (`sim_already_registered`), an identity already on another account (`kyc_id_in_use`) and a person at the policy's SIM limit (`id_cap_exceeded`, unless the policy allows the `id_cap_override` exception, which then needs a manager co-sign). Evidence images are slice R2b. Nothing here is a legal conclusion; capture no real customer data until counsel has answered.

Takes a queued registration for 15 minutes so two verifiers do not decide one item (`claimed_by_another` for the second). A claim is a soft lock: it lapses, and the decision itself is one conditional update under the registration's row lock. With the policy's separation of duties on, the capturer cannot claim (`separation_of_duties_required`).

Never edits a registration: it creates a NEW version that supersedes the approved one when it is approved, and the old record stays until then and afterwards (history is kept). The new version goes through the same verification. `reason` is one of a fixed list.

A manager's co-sign, for an allowed EXCEPTION only (`manager_cosign_for` in the policy), from a separate signed-in session: never a PIN. The manager must be neither the capturer nor the verifier and must manage the registration's store.

A manager REFUSES an exception that waits for a co-sign: the registration is turned down with one FIXED reason code (no free text) and its identity record is rejected unless another registration rests on it. Same rules as the co-sign: a manager of the registration's store, in a separate session, who is neither the capturer nor the verifier.

post.description: Adds one file of evidence to a registration that is still being captured, for the capturer's own store. Send the raw file (`image/png`, `image/jpeg` or `application/octet-stream`; at most 5 MiB) and the `kind` query value. The type is decided by the bytes (a declared type that contradicts them is refused). A PDF is refused (`evidence_pdf_not_supported`) without being parsed: send a photo or a screenshot. A picture is rewritten without its camera metadata (the camera time is kept as a timestamp for fraud checks); an oversized picture is refused. The file is sealed before it is stored. Refusals: `evidence_type_not_allowed`, `evidence_too_large`, `evidence_malformed`, `evidence_image_too_large`, `evidence_pdf_not_supported`, `evidence_window_closed` (the registration is claimed or decided), `evidence_limit_reached`. A camera input on the capture screen is advisory only: nothing about when or where a photo was taken is trusted. Nothing here is a legal conclusion; capture no real identity document until counsel has answered.

The person who captured the registration or added the file can never open it; after a decision only back office and the retail administrator can (`evidence_view_forbidden`, logged as a refusal).
